title: Review: Round 10 core/smtp/sieve-native/lmdb
notes:
## Section 5 — Triage

### P0 (Correctness bugs that break invariants)
- stoa-a805d881.1: backfill BFS unbounded — OOM via adversarial peer DAG

### P1 (Security / maintainer risk)
- stoa-a805d881.2: signing.rs TOCTOU — temp key file world-readable before chmod
- stoa-a805d881.3: sieve_admin user_exists case asymmetry with SMTP RCPT

### P2 (Efficiency)
- stoa-a805d881.4: rate_limiter O(n) eviction in hot path
- stoa-a805d881.5: sieve regex recompiled on every str_matches_regex_pat call

### P3/P4 — None filed
No genuine elegance or readability findings that survived the bikeshed filter.

## Section 6 — Decision Records (things done well)

- **Merkle-CRDT tip advancement is atomic**: advance_tips() wraps DELETE+INSERT in a single SQLite transaction. The reconcile loop has explicit MAX_HAVE=1000 and MAX_BFS_VISITS=5000 bounds; the backfill counterpart is what's missing (m9ua.1).
- **Type-enforced signature verification**: VerifiedEntry wrapper means callers cannot insert unverified entries — the type system prevents the mistake, not just documentation.
- **UNIQUE constraint → DuplicateEntry mapping**: insert_entry translates DB-level UNIQUE violations to DuplicateEntry without a TOCTOU window (no pre-check outside the transaction).
- **HLC overflow is hard-errored**: i64::try_from on hlc_timestamp at insert time returns a hard error rather than truncating silently; matching guard on read rejects negative stored timestamps.
- **Wildmat uses DP not backtracking regex**: O(n*m) with no catastrophic backtracking on adversarial patterns.
- **subtle::ConstantTimeEq for bearer tokens**: timing-safe comparison on admin API even for loopback listeners — correct defensive posture.
- **Rate limiter uses Mutex not RwLock**: both check and consume must be atomic; RwLock would introduce a TOCTOU window. Correct choice, even though the eviction scan is inefficient (m9ua.4).
- **Sieve delivery: reject-wins semantics**: if any recipient's Sieve script rejects, the whole delivery is rejected. Correct for mail integrity.
- **SMTP DATA body: too_large flag defers rejection until after dot-terminator**: RFC 5321 compliant; avoids connection-reset mid-message.
- **signing.rs: load_signing_key checks permissions before reading**: group-readable AND world-readable both rejected (0o044 mask). Correct.
- **DKIM/SPF/DMARC: never rejects on parse failure**: permerror is logged but not a rejection condition; avoids operator lockout on misconfigured DNS.

## Section 7 — Confidence Calibration

Coverage: read all files in crates/core/*, crates/smtp/*, crates/sieve-native/*, crates/lmdb/*.

High-confidence findings (code read line-by-line, confirmed):
- m9ua.1 (backfill BFS): confirmed no bound in the while loop at backfill.rs:105-150
- m9ua.2 (signing TOCTOU): confirmed File::create before set_permissions at signing.rs:134-141
- m9ua.3 (case asymmetry): confirmed == in sieve_admin user_exists vs eq_ignore_ascii_case in session.rs

Medium-confidence (behavior inferred from structure, not integration-tested):
- m9ua.4 (rate limiter O(n)): eviction logic observed; O(n) under adversarial IP churn is structural
- m9ua.5 (regex recompile): Regex::new in str_matches_regex_pat confirmed; PERF comment already present

Areas NOT covered (out of scope or not reachable from in-scope code):
- transit/ and reader/ binaries — call sites for backfill not reviewed
- Network protocol framing (below SMTP layer)
- SQLite schema migrations
- IPFS/LMDB integration paths above the lmdb crate interface

Round 10 review complete.
